title: The road to the Transformer
blurb: Sixty years from a machine that could not learn XOR to one that reads a sentence in a single parallel step. Each arrow is a limit somebody hit and what they did about it.

title: Making networks deep enough to matter
blurb: The convolutional architecture was settled in 1980; everything after is about getting gradients through more layers than the last attempt could manage.

title: An architecture crosses domains
blurb: Attention was built for translation. Cutting an image into patches let the same block read pictures — and the smallness of that change is the argument.

title: Learning to generate
blurb: Compress, then sample. From an autoencoder that only reconstructs, through adversarial training, to diffusion — three answers to the same question about where new images come from.

title: How diffusion overtook GANs
blurb: Adversarial training gave sharp images and unstable optimisation. Score matching gave a likelihood and a slow sampler. The line that won traded one for the other, then made it fast.

title: From value functions to language models
blurb: Reinforcement learning spent thirty years on games, and then its policy-gradient machinery turned out to be how you make a language model follow instructions.

title: Teaching a model what was wanted
blurb: Predicting the next token is not the same as being useful. The last three steps are about the difference, and about doing it without a reward model at all.

title: Getting pictures and words into one space
blurb: Captioning taught a network to describe an image. Contrastive pretraining taught it to put images and sentences in the same coordinates, which is what made everything since possible.
